clue.text: Allowed motoring organisation back in the ring

indicators.note: back tells us the two pieces together are to be read from the end to the start

parts.note: let means allowed, as in 'let them in'
the RAC is the Royal Automobile Club, a British motoring organisation

explanation.surface: A drivers' club seems to be returning to the boxing ring after being permitted.
explanation.walkthrough: The RAC is the Royal Automobile Club, a British breakdown and motoring body.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring is a group of traders conspiring to fix prices, which is exactly what a cartel is.

clue.text: Solo passage can daze terribly

indicators.note: terribly suggests something done badly, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written: these two words supply the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A performer's solo stretch is so bad it can stun the listener.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadenza is a virtuoso section for the soloist alone in a concerto movement.

clue.text: Run out to right part of machine

parts.note: R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for a run
O stands for out, as in cricket scorecards
taken as written

explanation.surface: A worker is sent out to the right-hand component of some machinery.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotor is the spinning component in engines, pumps and helicopters.

clue.text: Without any limit to the development of north and south Leeds

indicators.note: development implies change, so the letters that follow are reshaped into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Planners promise unlimited growth across the northern and southern parts of Leeds.
explanation.walkthrough: Leeds is a city in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Something endless goes on with no boundary or finish, i.e. it is unbounded.

clue.text: Supported British leading player on the day

parts.note: an ace is a top performer, a star of the side

explanation.surface: A British star was backed up by teammates on match day.
explanation.definitionFit: Braced means propped up or reinforced, as a wall is held by struts.

clue.text: Hangover time for the old widow

parts.note: a relic is something surviving from the past, a hangover from earlier times

explanation.surface: An elderly widow is nursing a hangover at this hour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hangover' suggests too much drink, but here it means a leftover from the past.
explanation.definitionFit: Relict is an archaic word for a surviving spouse, hence the 'old' in the clue.

clue.text: Got chirpy about legal claim

indicators.note: about can mean turned around or moved about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written: these words supply the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone became cheerful about a lawsuit they had filed.
explanation.definitionFit: Copyright is the legal right of ownership over creative work, a claim the law enforces.

clue.text: Loses light boat: send another outside

indicators.note: the reworked letters go outside, wrapping round the boat
another version of the word send means its letters rearranged into a different form

parts.note: taken as written: the word itself supplies the letters to rearrange
Noah's ark is the most famous boat

explanation.surface: A boat lamp fails, so someone orders a replacement to be sent out.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that darkens grows dimmer, gradually going without illumination.

clue.text: Omits to include looseness in order to limit the damage

indicators.note: to include means the first word wraps around the rearranged letters

parts.note: to cut is to leave out, so cuts means omits

indicators.note: putting something in order means arranging it, so the letters of looseness are sorted afresh

parts.note: taken as written: the word itself supplies the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: An editor drops slack material so as to keep the harm down.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut one's losses is the idiom for abandoning a failing venture before it costs even more.

clue.text: Check on finances, excluding university entrance

indicators.note: excluding signals that a letter is left out of the word

parts.note: an audit is an official inspection of accounts

explanation.surface: An accounts inspection that leaves out a university's admissions office.
explanation.definitionFit: An adit is a horizontal passage into a mine, its way in.

clue.text: Leave car in second row to have large gin, maybe, at pleasure garden

parts.note: a double is a twice-sized measure of spirits, gin being one example
a park is a public garden for recreation

explanation.surface: A driver blocks the street to go and drink a big gin at an amusement garden.
explanation.definitionFit: To double-park is to stop a vehicle alongside cars already parked at the kerb.

clue.text: Freedom of access as a matter of course

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the right or privilege of admission somewhere
second meaning: a dish served at a meal, i.e. one course of it

explanation.walkthrough: 'A matter of course' reads as 'something routine', but it means a course at dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: The French-derived word covers both admission to a circle and a dish at a meal (a main dish in the US, a starter in Britain).

clue.text: Happened that the officer made better run in

parts.note: OC is short for Officer Commanding

indicators.note: in tells us the run letter goes inside the word for healed

parts.note: cured means healed, made better

explanation.surface: It came about that the commander's healing let a soldier run again.
explanation.definitionFit: Occurred means took place, came about.

clue.text: Does he want one's support for camping?

definitions.text: Does he want one's support for camping?

parts.note: reads as someone seeking votes or backing from the public
but camping hints at tents, made of heavy canvas fabric

explanation.walkthrough: The seeker of support is one who goes door to door for votes; the tent fabric gives the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: A canvasser solicits votes or opinions, and the word contains canvas, the tent material.

clue.text: Roman writer had no right to bet on a Guardian Angel

indicators.note: had no means the writer's name lacks the letter for right

parts.note: Virgil was the Roman poet who wrote the Aeneid
an ante is a stake put in before a poker hand

explanation.surface: A Latin poet without principles gambles on a heavenly protector.
explanation.walkthrough: The Guardian Angels are a volunteer street-patrol group, so a member is a self-appointed crime fighter.
explanation.definitionFit: A vigilante takes law enforcement into their own hands, as the Guardian Angels patrols do.

clue.text: Lengthy periods when holding back, for example

indicators.note: holding means the word for when wraps around the other piece

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

indicators.note: back means the abbreviation is read from right to left

explanation.surface: Long stretches pass while someone holds back, for instance.
explanation.definitionFit: Ages are long spans of time, as in 'I waited for ages'.

clue.text: Long story of finding silver in South Africa

indicators.note: in places the chemical symbol inside the country's abbreviation

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A lengthy tale of striking silver in South Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: A saga is a long narrative, originally a Norse heroic tale.

clue.text: Fish for the main singer

parts.note: the main is a poetic term for the open sea
a bass is a singer with the lowest male voice

explanation.surface: Seafood intended for the lead vocalist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The main' looks like 'the principal', but here it is the old word for the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: Sea bass is a common edible marine species.

clue.text: One taking action in straightforward quarrel

parts.note: plain means simple, straightforward
a tiff is a minor squabble

explanation.surface: Someone becomes involved in a simple row.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaintiff brings a lawsuit, i.e. takes legal action against someone.

clue.text: Stalemate causes awful spasm? That is the case

indicators.note: being the case means the abbreviation forms a casing round the jumbled letters

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

indicators.note: awful indicates the letters are mangled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written: the word itself supplies the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A deadlock brings on a dreadful muscle cramp, and that is how it is.
explanation.definitionFit: An impasse is a deadlock where no progress is possible.

clue.text: People held by strange gift of imagination, perhaps

definitions.note: the phrase 'a figment of the imagination' supplies the sense; the definition hints at that idiom

indicators.note: held by means the people are enclosed within the reworked letters
strange signals the letters of gift turned into an odd new order

parts.note: taken as written: the word itself supplies the letters to rearrange
men can stand for people in general

explanation.surface: People are caught up in a weird talent for invention.
explanation.definitionFit: A figment is an invented thing, best known in the phrase 'a figment of the imagination'.

clue.text: Rush for transport: always five short

parts.note: a car is a means of transport

indicators.note: short means lacking, so the word goes without the Roman numeral

parts.note: ever means always, as in 'ever hopeful'
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: A dash for a vehicle, with five passengers always missing.
explanation.definitionFit: To career is to hurtle along at speed, out of control.

clue.text: Feel poorly with bright lights around the train systems

indicators.note: around tells us the beams of light surround the other pieces

parts.note: rays are beams of light
to ail is to be unwell

explanation.surface: Feeling unwell under the glare of floodlights at a train station.
explanation.definitionFit: Railways are networks of tracks along which trains run.

clue.text: Promise drunk to in hock?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: as a verb, to ... someone is to drink their health, so this is the past form of that sense
third meaning: goods in ... are pawned, in hock

explanation.walkthrough: Three meanings of one word: a vow, a toast, and something pawned; 'in hock' means held by a pawnbroker.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers a vow, a toast to someone's health and an item deposited as security for a loan.

clue.text: Keen on music? Oddly show lack of interest

indicators.note: oddly signals taking letters at regular intervals, here every other letter of the phrase

parts.note: the run of letters from which every second one is taken, starting with the second

explanation.surface: A music lover strangely shows no enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters are the 2nd, 4th, 6th and so on; 'oddly' here means irregularly rather than the odd positions.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is listless boredom, a weariness from want of anything exciting.

clue.text: They provide washing for money

parts.note: reads as a laundry service doing clothes for a fee
but money laundering is cleaning dirty cash through legitimate business

explanation.walkthrough: On the surface they clean clothes for pay; the other reading is criminals who clean illicit money.
explanation.definitionFit: Launderers wash linen, and money launderers disguise the source of illegal funds.

clue.text: Want daughter to be born first

indicators.note: first means the word for born comes before the daughter letter

parts.note: née marks a woman's maiden name, born as

explanation.surface: Wishing for a daughter to arrive first.
explanation.definitionFit: To need something is to require or lack it, i.e. to want it.

clue.text: Make a mistake in retiring with drink

indicators.note: in puts the slip-up inside the bashful word

parts.note: retiring means shy, reserved
to err is to go wrong

explanation.surface: Someone blunders at bedtime over a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retiring' suggests going to bed, but it means bashful.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherry is a fortified wine from southern Spain.

clue.text: Clear half the street

parts.note: demi- is a prefix meaning half
ST is the usual abbreviation for street in addresses

explanation.surface: Tidy up half of the road.
explanation.definitionFit: To demist is to clear condensation from a windscreen or window.
